key: Saran A, White H, Kuper H. Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2020,16(1):e1070 || Corrigendum published July 12, 2020 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(3):e1104, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1104). The corrigendum corrected the income-country distribution figure: the original text 'over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from upper-middle income countries' was changed to 'almost half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries, closely followed by upper-middle income countries (n=48).' The figure for low-income countries (n=9) was retained

key: Kuper H, Saran A, White H. Rapid Evidence Assessment (REA) of What Works to Improve Educational Outcomes for People with Disabilities in Low- and Middle-Income Countries. Campbell Collaboration and International Centre for Evidence in Disability. 2018 || The 2018 REA was a precursor to the 2025 Hunt et al. systematic review, which PubMed records as an update of the associated protocol. No separate update to the REA itself was found, it has been functionally superseded by the 2025 full systematic review

key: Ahmed SK, Jeffries D, Chakraborty A, et al. Teacher professional development for disability inclusion in low- and middle-income Asia-Pacific countries: An evidence and gap map. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2022,18(4):e1287 || A corrigendum (e1315, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1315) was published February 25, 2023 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 19(1):e1315). The draft itself acknowledges this correction exists but states it could not read it. Despite this, the draft proceeds to cite multiple specific figures from the uncorrected version of the map. The content of the corrigendum could not be fully retrieved from available search results, so it is not possible to confirm whether the specific figures the draft uses (50 studies, 16 countries, three mental health studies, no positive-behaviour studies) were among those corrected
